item.description:

Short Description:
Validates that user-defined data sources grouped under platforms currently return at least one event, recording PASS/FAIL/ERROR/STALE status per source.


Description:
The Data Source Validator app validates that user-defined data sources are currently returning at least one event in Splunk. Administrators define platforms such as Firewall or EDR, and under each platform create one or more data sources with an SPL search that should return events. A single sequential validation worker executes each data source's search on a schedule or on demand using a dedicated service account with minimal privileges. The app records PASS, FAIL, ERROR, or STALE status for each data source, and platform status rolls up from the status of its enabled child data sources. This provides visibility into which integrations have stopped receiving data. The app targets Splunk Cloud Platform and Splunk Enterprise 9.3 and later.

Users without the mcp\_tool\_admin capability see the Create tool button disabled. **Role-Based Access Control for MCP Tools** MCP tools now support role-based access control, ensuring tools are only accessible to users with the appropriate roles and permissions. **App Parameter in run\_splunk\_query** Added an app parameter to run\_splunk\_query tool arguments, allowing users to specify the app context for query execution. **Saved Search Descriptions in Knowledge Objects** The get\_knowledge\_objects tool now returns saved search descriptions when querying saved searches. **Workload Management Support for run\_splunk\_query** MCP tool run\_splunk\_query now supports Splunk workload pool assignment for better resource management. **SAIA Data Discovery Tool** Added a new SAIA data discovery tool. This tool requires Splunk AI Assistant version 2.2.0 or later. **MCP Dashboard Updates** Added a new tools and roles panel in the Governance tab to show tool access by role. **UI Updates** MCP version is now displayed on the Configuration page. Added MCP Tool Annotations to identify read-only and write-capable tools. Row limit and Time range rows are no longer shown per tool. Users cannot set a per-tool rate limit beyond the global rate limit. Users cannot set the global rate limit below an existing per-tool rate limit. Added an MCP Server heartbeat modular input to prevent Splunk from recycling the MCP handler process. **Issues Fixed** Fixed an issue where custom \`mcp.conf\` settings were not replicated correctly across search head cluster members. **Notes and Considerations** Administrators who previously managed SPL command restrictions through manual configuration should review the new Allowed SPL Commands section in the Guardrails tab.


Description:
MCP Server for Splunk Platform The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard and framework that enables seamless, secure, and standardized two-way communication between AI applications (like large language models) and external data sources or tools. It acts as a universal adapter allowing AI systems to access, execute, and integrate functionalities from diverse systems through a common protocol, simplifying data sharing and tool interoperability without custom coding for each integration. Splunk's Model Context Protocol (MCP) server leverages this to provide a standardized, secure, and scalable interface to connect AI assistants, agents, and other intelligent systems with data in the Splunk platform for both Enterprise & Cloud customers in beta. 🔑 Key Features - Universal Connectivity Seamlessly connects AI agents and tools to Splunk data resources in a secure and efficient manner. - Enterprise-Grade Security Includes built-in authentication, authorization, and Role-Based Access Control (RBAC). - Rapid Deployment Offers a plug-and-play solution, eliminating the need for custom integrations. ⚙️ Core Capabilities - Explore the Data Navigate and interact with Splunk data effortlessly. - Discover Knowledge Objects Identify and access relevant saved searches, lookups, and other knowledge assets. - Execute Searches Run powerful Splunk queries to extract insights and drive intelligent workflows. - Leverage AI capabilities from Splunk’s AI Assistant for SPL & MLTK SPL search generation from natural language, search optimization, search explanation, retrieve MLTK models and algorithms.

item.title: Federal AI LookupOps - v1.0.1 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
Version 1.0.1 - reliability and compatibility fixes. Forward compatibility: restmap.conf now declares python.required (3.9, 3.13) alongside python.version, clearing the Splunk 10.2+ deprecation of python.version. No change to supported versions - the app still targets Splunk Enterprise 9.1 through 10.x, search heads only, and python.required is ignored below 10.2. Write path fixes: * Settings and record writes now use the correct splunkd request transport and KV Store upsert semantics, so first-time writes (including the initial settings save on a fresh install) succeed. * \- The app REST endpoint is now exposed at all nested route depths, so the full change workflow (validate, approve, publish, roll back) resolves through Splunk Web. * \- Request bodies are delivered reliably through Splunk Web's proxy. * \- The audit hash-chain tip is resolved deterministically, independent of KV Store sort ordering. Install and first-use fixes: * Removed a setup gate that could leave a fresh install unable to reach the app views. The Setup page remains available from the navigation bar. * \- A brand-new lookup with no existing baseline now diffs cleanly instead of surfacing a raw splunkd error. Validated on Splunk Enterprise 9.4 with KV Store; AppInspect clean. Requires a Splunk restart after install to register the REST handler and KV Store collections.


Short Description:
Air-gap-first governance for Splunk lookup changes: inventory, deterministic validation, semantic diff, approvals with separation of duties, verified publication and rollback, audit evidence export, offline transfer bundles, and optional behind-the-firewall AI review with zero authority. No cloud dependencies. No telemetry.


Description:
Federal AI LookupOps turns Splunk lookup edits into governed changes. It is built air-gap-first: no cloud dependencies, no external services, and no telemetry. Analysts propose candidate changes by uploading a CSV, pasting records, or cloning the current lookup. A deterministic policy engine validates schemas, unique and composite keys, field types (IPv4, IPv6, CIDR, hostname, URL, email, date, boolean, number), enumerations, patterns, blank values, duplicates, and expirations. A key-aware semantic diff shows exactly what will change - additions, removals, field-level modifications, normalization-only changes, and schema changes - each with a stable evidence ID. Approvers act under enforced separation of duties; self-approval is blocked server-side. Publication captures the production content hash at submission, re-verifies it immediately before the write, publishes only through documented Splunk interfaces, verifies the resulting hash after the write, and preserves the previous version for one-action verified rollback. Every step lands in a hash-chained audit trail with an exportable JSON evidence report. Deterministic offline bundles with SHA-256 manifests move changes safely between enclaves. Optionally, connect a customer-approved, behind-the-firewall LLM (OpenAI-compatible, Ollama, or custom JSON). AI review runs server-side only with TLS verification always enforced, and provides risk assessment, justification-vs-diff contradiction detection, reviewer questions, policy proposals, normalization patches, dependency impact, and release narratives. Every material AI finding must cite deterministic evidence IDs, and the model has zero authority - it can never approve, publish, or roll back. Works with your existing SAML login through Splunk's own authentication. Includes role-based capabilities (view, submit, approve, publish, rollback, AI use, AI admin), KV Store-backed state that replicates across search-head clusters, and full documentation. Support: LC@federal.ai | www.federal.ai

item.title: Supporting App for Oracle SBC CDR - v0.9.0 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
**Version 0.9.0 (July 22nd, 2026)** - **IMPORTANT / BREAKING CHANGE:** The Oracle SBC media-flow fields have been renamed to align with Oracle's own terminology. The old "west", "east", "extra_west" and "extra_east" field-name prefixes were a nonstandard naming scheme that did not appear anywhere in Oracle's documentation. The new names map to Oracle's flow-set and flow-direction concepts — Flow-Set 1 or 2 (fs1 / fs2), and Forward or Reverse (fwd / rev). For the media flow and quality-of-service fields the mapping is: - `west_*` → `fs1_fwd_*` (Flow-Set 1, Forward direction) - `east_*` → `fs1_rev_*` (Flow-Set 1, Reverse direction) - `extra_*` → `fs2_fwd_*` / `fs2_rev_*` (Flow-Set 2, Forward / Reverse) A few groups of fields do not follow that prefix pattern exactly: the media-stop-time and RTP transmitted-byte/packet counters are indexed by flow-set and calling/called party, and the session R-Factor and MOS values are now simply `calling_r_factor`, `calling_mos`, `called_r_factor` and `called_mos` (they are session-level, not per-flow). If you have built any of your own saved searches, dashboards, or reports that reference the old field names, you will need to update them when you upgrade. - Added a new search command, `| checksbcflowfieldnames`, to make that migration easy and exact. Run it (as an admin, or as a user with the `admin_all_objects` capability, for a complete picture) and it will itemize every place in your Splunk knowledge objects, ie saved searches, dashboards, macros, event types, data models, etc, that still reference any old field name, giving you the precise new name to use for each one. - Call detail view for Oracle SBC calls now includes a single-row summary table at the top echoing top level details like ingress/egress realm, time, disposition and duration etc. - Call detail view for Oracle SBC calls now includes a CallFlowGraph module that presents a DAG visualization of the various ip addresses and ingress/egress realms involved in the B2BUA signaling and media flow.


Description:
This app provides the Splunk configuration to ingest the CDR data from Oracle SBC. It is intended to work for both Oracle Session Router CDR and Oracle SBC CDR, although some unknowns remain as of this writing. It is also designed to work as a Supporting App alongside Sideview's commercial "Cisco CDR Reporting and Analytics" app. When used in conjunction with the Cisco CDR app, the Oracle SBC data can be used in that app alongside the CUCM data.

## Initial Preview release This is the first public release of the NetFlow and SNMP Analytics for Splunk (Preview) app: a ground-up redesign of NetFlow Logic's Splunk app, rebuilt on Dashboard Studio in dark mode. item.title: Data Heartbeat - v1.9.0 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Short Description:
Know the moment a data source goes silent. Data Heartbeat monitors every source type in your Splunk environment and fires Slack, Teams, webhook, or email alerts the instant data stops flowing — before gaps turn into blind spots.


Description:
Data Heartbeat monitors your Splunk environment for source types that have stopped sending data. When a data source goes silent — whether from a misconfigured forwarder, a failed log shipper, or a broken integration — Data Heartbeat detects the gap and alerts you before the silence becomes a blind spot. Every monitored source type has a configurable threshold, measured in minutes. When no data arrives within that window, the app flags the source type and fires your chosen alert action: Slack, Microsoft Teams, a generic webhook, or email via Splunk's built-in SMTP relay. Key features: • Monitor dashboard — a live status table showing every tracked source type, the minutes since its last event, its threshold, and its importance level, with color-coded severity (green, yellow, red, and critical). • Per-row alert actions — each source type can use its own notification target, independent of the global default. • Auto Discovery — a nightly scan that surfaces new source types appearing in your environment and queues them for review. • Importance tagging — mark business-critical sources as High, Medium, or Low importance. When a high-importance source goes silent, the app raises a red-alert banner. • Settings page — configure global defaults (threshold, alert action, and notification target), enable or disable the monitoring pipeline, and test alert actions without waiting for a real outage. • Audit log — a full history of every configuration change, with timestamps and user attribution. • No index footprint — all configuration is stored in KV Store, so no custom indexes are required. Data Heartbeat is compatible with Splunk Enterprise 8.2+, Splunk Cloud Classic, and Splunk Cloud Victoria.

Description:
The NetKit Add-on collects network probe telemetry - TCP connect latency, internet throughput, and TLS certificate health - from full Splunk Enterprise instances, emitting the results as JSON events ready for network monitoring. It runs three probes, all implemented in pure Python on the standard library with no external binaries or third-party dependencies. Ping probes measure TCP connect latency by timing the handshake to each host:port target, never using ICMP. Speedtest probes measure download and upload throughput plus latency against Cloudflare endpoints over verified HTTPS connections. TLS probes connect to each target, verify the presented certificate against the system CA store or a configured private CA, and record certificate identity, validity periods, and verification status. Events are written with the sourcetypes netkit:ping, netkit:speedtest, and netkit:tls, while probe execution logs are captured to the _internal index as netkit_log. item.title: WithSecure Elements Add-on - v1.0.6 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
**⚠️ Critical bug fix. Recommended upgrade for anyone running v1.0.2 through v1.0.5.** ## The bug `advance_ts` used a `strptime` call with a hard-coded `.%f` format directive, which raises `ValueError` when the WithSecure Elements API returns a timestamp without fractional seconds. Both forms are valid ISO 8601 and both are returned by the API depending on the event: ``` 2026-07-22T11:19:08.804Z ← parsed correctly 2026-07-22T11:19:08Z ← ValueError ! ``` The exception was raised inside `_set_checkpoint`, so the polling cursor never advanced past that timestamp. Every subsequent polling cycle re-fetched the same window and re-indexed the same events, producing an ever-growing pile of duplicates in the target index. ## Who is affected * The bug has existed since **v1.0.2 (June 2026)**. Every version from v1.0.2 to v1.0.5 is affected. * It only manifests when the **last event of a fetched batch** happens to have no fractional seconds — which is why it was not caught earlier in testing. About one third of the events in the reporter's environment turned out to be in that form. * **Symptom**: continuously growing duplicate ingestion for `withsecure:epp:security_event`, `withsecure:epp:bcd_incident`, and/or `withsecure:epp:bcd_detection`. ## The fix * New helper `parse_iso_utc` in `withsecure_api.py` uses `datetime.fromisoformat` after rewriting the trailing `Z` as `+00:00`. Handles both timestamp forms natively on Python 3.9+. * `parse_iso_utc` also normalises the result to a **timezone-aware UTC** datetime, so any downstream arithmetic or formatting is unambiguous even if a future API revision were to return a non-UTC offset. * `utc_iso` now converts a tz-aware input to UTC before formatting, so the trailing literal `Z` always reflects the actual UTC instant. * `advance_ts` (`withsecure_api.py`) and `_parse_iso` (`withsecure_locks.py`) both use the new helper — a single source of truth for ISO 8601 parsing across the add-on. ## What to do after upgrading If you were affected by duplicates on a previous version, the duplicates already in the index remain (Splunk does not rewrite past events). New events indexed after v1.0.6 will be clean. To de-duplicate at search time until historical events roll off retention: ``` index=main sourcetype="withsecure:epp:security_event" | dedup id sortby -_time ``` Similar patterns for `withsecure:epp:bcd_incident` (`dedup incidentId,updatedTimestamp`) and `withsecure:epp:bcd_detection` (`dedup detectionId`). ## Upgrade safety Non-destructive in-place upgrade when installed via Splunk's standard "Install app from file → Upgrade app" workflow (or `splunk install app -update 1`): * existing KV Store checkpoints are preserved → polling picks up right where it left off, no historical re-fetch * existing input configuration in `local/inputs.conf` (credentials, intervals, filters, proxy settings) is preserved * no scheme or config changes → no user action required ## Compatibility * Splunk Enterprise / Cloud: **9.0, 9.1, 9.2, 9.3, 9.4, 10.0, 10.1, 10.2, 10.3, 10.4, 10.5** * CIM: 4.x, 5.x, 6.x, 8.x * Python: 3.9+ * Splunk KV Store: enabled


Short Description:
Collects EPP Security Events and EDR Broad Context Detections from WithSecure Elements via OAuth2-authenticated API, with CIM-compliant field extractions for endpoint, malware, intrusion detection, and process data.


Description:
The WithSecure Elements Add-on collects endpoint protection and detection data from the WithSecure Elements API. It ingests EPP Security Events and EDR Broad Context Detections through OAuth2-authenticated modular inputs, enabling centralized security event analysis in Splunk. The add-on maps collected events to CIM endpoint, malware, intrusion detection, and process tags, facilitating correlation with other security data sources. Two modular inputs handle data collection: withsecure_epp_input retrieves endpoint protection events, while withsecure_bcd_input collects EDR broad context detection incidents. Events are indexed under source types withsecure:epp:security_event, withsecure:epp:bcd_incident, and withsecure:epp:bcd_detection. The add-on includes a custom search command for retrieving specific detection details and provides a workflow action to fetch incident detections directly from the Splunk interface.

**What's new in TA Studio 1.6.0** - Open any packaged add-on (AOB/UCC/plain-conf) by uploading it straight from your browser — no server paths or permissions to configure - Imported add-ons open editable, with View source for any externally-written handler - New Code Files editor with AI assist for custom collectors and alert helpers - Dashboard Studio support, alongside Classic Simple XML - Reconciliation for opened add-ons that contradict their own configuration - Managed, pinned build toolchain (ucc-gen + AppInspect), with optional version overrides and offline/manual install guidance - Redesigned Settings page - Pre-build problem detection — catches build blockers in seconds, not minutes - Many Splunk-vendor add-ons (AWS, Microsoft) now import, build, and run - Date fields no longer show "Invalid date"; Help Links can now be clickable links - New inputs appear in "Create New Input" for add-ons with a curated menu; file-upload fields on setup pages now build - …and many more bug fixes and small feature additions


Short Description:
Build, import, validate, and package Splunk add-ons through a visual browser UI — no CLI. Create inputs (REST/shell/Python), alert actions, source types, field extractions, CIM mappings, lookups, and setup pages on the UCC Framework, run inputs and alerts in the browser to inspect their output, validate with AppInspect, and package for Splunkbase in one click.


Description:
TA Studio is a browser-based visual workbench for building Splunk® add-ons (TAs) on the Universal Configuration Console (UCC) Framework — without touching the command line. Authoring a quality add-on normally means working with the ucc-gen CLI, hand-editing globalConfig.json and a web of .conf files, and running AppInspect and packaging from a terminal. TA Studio replaces that workflow with a guided, point-and-click interface that runs entirely inside your own Splunk instance. From one UI you can create and manage data inputs (REST API, shell command, or Python modular inputs), alert actions (including Enterprise Security adaptive response), source types, field extractions with a live regex builder, CIM data model mappings, setup pages (accounts, proxy, logging), CSV lookups, and event types. You can import existing Splunk Add-on Builder and conf-based add-ons to modernize them, run inputs and alert actions right in the browser to inspect the events and output they produce, validate with AppInspect (including cloud checks) and review the results, then package a Splunkbase-ready archive in one click. TA Studio also includes built-in AI assistance to help you generate and refine input and alert-action code as you work. It otherwise runs entirely within your local Splunk environment: your add-on projects are not collected, transmitted, or stored outside your instance, and AI features send only the content you choose to submit to your selected AI provider.
